I have 4 problems with his proposals:

1) One order gives mental health professionals the mandate to report concerning clients to the FBI without fear of prosecution. Therapists can already contact LE in cases of threat to the patient or someone else, but with this order could very easily simply ensure that none of their clients can own guns because they have a personal problem with guns. It also gives therapists dangerous extrajudicial leverage over patients (no prosecution statutes are inherently bad). While this provision exists, none of us should consider seeking professional counseling, or allow anyone we love to do so either. The concern is not necessarily that this keeps people from being able to buy guns, but that the "list" this order will generate is not something that any living person should ever want to be on. There's a reason that until now no one has ever thought it a good idea for private mental health data to be given to the Federal Government for decisions involving the restriction of guaranteed rights. The end result can't be any better than the No-Fly List, except that the dialogue about the gun list will be that "only crazy people are on it." This move very much hurts mental health in this country, which is one of the biggest possible steps backward.

2) While it's a fantastic idea to close the "gun show loophole," it has to be done in a way that doesn't yank the rug out from under existing people with stock. Some folks have built up inventories that they move from show to show to sell, and adding $35+ new transfer fees for each firearm negates their profits. I can't abide a law that fucks people's well-laid plans up when it doesn't necessarily have to. Give these folks some time to exit their legitimate businesses without losing everything they've built. Saying "next month" to force fast legal showdowns is just a dick move, especially in good old incrementalist America.

3) Many guns aren't WORTH the $35+ transfer fees these Orders will demand. Forcing someone to use an FFL every time they flip a .25 for $60 is going to ensure that 100% of guns under $100 become illegal in very short order. Worse, if someone owns a cheap gun that they now can't get rid of, that gun will not be respected and is more likely to be stolen, misplaced, or simply thrown in the garbage. Any executive order or law making all gun sales pass through the FBI needs to significantly decrease the price of the background check and ideally increase the availability of those checks outside of the private sector. If police departments can't do them for $10 or 10% of the gun sales price (whichever is cheaper) in a booth near their "Cragslist Zones," normal law abiding people are just going to laugh at this law and make jokes about what kind of criminals they are over gun deals in their backyards.

4) Many families have gun collections which are passed from generation to generation. If I have to pay $35 on every gun my Grandpa is going to leave me I'm going to have to take out a monster loan or own a huge cache of illegal weapons. Yay.
